title: ship's changed-path staging fails on a staged RENAME — git add of the old half errors 'did not match any files'
evidence: Live 2026-07-27 (hotfix ship c21dcb0b prep): with a rename staged (.evolve/inbox/X.json -> .evolve/inbox/consumed/X.json, porcelain status 'R'), evolve ship --class manual FAILed [GIT_STAGE_FAILED/transient @atomic-ship]: ship re-derives changed paths from porcelain and runs git add per path, but the R line's OLD path no longer exists on disk and its deletion is already fully staged, so git add rejects the pathspec (rc=128). Worked around by setting status.renames=false for the ship (porcelain then reports plain D + A, both addable) and unsetting after.
notes: Fix in ship's porcelain parsing: an R-status line carries 'old -> new'; stage the deletion of old via git rm --cached semantics or simply split R into (D old, A new) before the per-path git add — or pass --no-renames to the status invocation ship already owns (one flag, no parse change; gitexec.PorcelainPath is the SSOT for the path extraction and R lines embed TWO paths, which is also a latent PorcelainPath hazard worth a test). Same class as the 1098 staging onion (absolute pathspec rc=128, ignored-path rc=1): ship staging must be total over every porcelain status code.
acceptance: RED first: a staged rename in the tree; evolve ship --class manual (dry-run path or test harness) stages and commits it without GIT_STAGE_FAILED.
PorcelainPath (or ship's caller) handles the 'R old -> new' two-path shape explicitly, with a test.
No behavior change for plain A/M/D paths.
cd go && go test -race ./internal/ship/... N/N PASS.
